clips.send: Someone sends it to a skeptical friend who thinks manifesting is nonsense: real lab proof that focused thought shifted a random machine - pure awe.
clips.caption:
A machine spits out random 1s and 0s - literally a coin flip, coded. Left alone, run it a billion times and it lands right around 49.9% to 50.1%. Never quite 50/50, but close.

Researchers sat someone in front of it and told them to just think '1' more than '0.'

The next run wasn't 50.1%. It was 51%, 52% - far enough outside the normal range that researchers called it a complete anomaly.

Kevin Trudeau calls this empirical evidence that a quiet, focused thought can shift a random outcome.

If thought can move a random number generator, what else has it been moving in your life?

clips.send: A friend sends it to someone grinding for one huge breakthrough: proof a tiny edge, not a giant one, is what actually pays 50x - awe and envy.
clips.caption:
Two horses cross the finish line. One wins by a nose - an inch, maybe a centimeter.

The winner doesn't get paid double for that tiny edge. Kevin Trudeau points out he gets paid 50 times more than the horse that came in second, even though he didn't run 50 times faster.

That's the whole point about luck: it was never about being better by a mile. It's about shifting the outcome just enough, right at the moment it counts.

There's an older book, Kevin says, that dozens of Hollywood stars credit with that exact edge.

What's the one small edge you've been ignoring?
